page.layout: Page number top left; running head across the top; two round portrait medallions side by side above the text, each with its inscription around the rim; one column of text with two paragraphs; a printer's woodcut ornament below the text. No margin notes.

main_text.p: IVVENALIS Aquinas, Poëta insignis, discipulus fuit Frontini Grammatici, qui quidem scripsit quinque libros satyrarum, sed non inveniuntur, quod eorum iactura sit facta, exceptis sexdecim satyris, in lucem ubique editis, propter magnam authoris celebritatem, in eo versus genere, in quo, Lucilio caeterisque Poëtis Satyricis, qui ad hoc usque tempus fuerūt, longè acrior fuisse palàm est omnibus. Vixit tempore Martialis, cum quo maxima ei intercessit familiaritas. Obiit in Ægypto 80. annis natus, floruitque circiter annum mundi 4060. & Christi 100. Vide Gesnerum in sua Bibliotheca..

GALENVS Pergami natus, patre Nicone insigni geometra & architecto divite, cuius praeceptor fuit Pelops, ut ipse testatur libro quarto de Locis affectis capite 7. & in libr. de Atra bile. Vixit Romae temporibus Traiani, Cōmodi & Antonini Pij Imperatorum anno mundi 4100. salutis vero humanae 140. Plurima scripsit in Geometria, Dialectica, Rhetorica, Philosophia, maximè vero in Medicina. Itaque Averroes in S. Collect. illum omnibus medicis anteferre non dubitavit. Vixit annos 70. secundum Suidam: alij 140. annos asserunt, ut testatur Coelius lib. 16. Antiq. lect. cap. 40. In patria tandem fatis cessit.

page.notes: Medallion inscriptions: the small rotated letters on the left side of the right-hand medallion are too small and worn to read: [illegible, ~3 letters]. The woodcut ornament below the text carries no printed words and is not transcribed. Running head and paragraph spelling follow the print, with u/v corrected as per the rules. Printed ligatures (ct, ft) are written as ct/ft, not as Latin look-alikes. The printed "16." after "lib." in the Coelius reference is copied as printed.
